events.feedback: The Critique: What’s Missing & What Needs FixingMissing a Mind-Blowing Local Connection: Right across the water from the park, in St. Petersburg, local history boasts the largest tree nest ever recorded for any animal species—a legendary bald eagle nest that measured 9.5 feet wide, 20 feet deep, and weighed nearly 3 tons (6,000 lbs). This local "wow factor" is perfect for park visitors.The Inverted Southern Nesting Season: The current draft mentions peak nesting from fall through spring, but it misses a fascinating biological detail: unlike northern eagles that nest in spring/summer, Florida eagles invert their schedule to beat the heat. events.summary: Seven fields updated to incorporate the reviewer's three substantive additions — the St. Petersburg world-record nest (dimensions and weight verified against USFWS and Guinness), Florida's status as one of the densest eagle concentrations in the lower 48 (FWC language), and the inverted fall-winter nesting calendar (FWC Biology and Audubon Florida EagleWatch). The reviewer's 'nearly 3 tons' weight figure was corrected to USFWS's 'almost 6,000 pounds'; 'White-headed Sea Eagle' was not added to also_known_as as it is a name for a different Eurasian species; and the migration detail was refined per FWC (it is subadults and non-breeders, not all nesting adults, that head north for summer).
